stem: When teaching wound-care infection prevention after transplantation, which hand-hygiene step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Wash hands before and after touching wounds or mucous membranes
Hand-washing is needed only after wound care, not before
Gloves alone replace all hand-washing around wounds
Wound-contact hand hygiene applies only in the hospital

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipient hand-hygiene teaching includes washing hands before and after touching wounds or mucous membranes, along with washing after secretions, bathroom use, and animal contact.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hand-washing is recommended both before and after wound or mucous membrane contact.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hand-washing with soap and water remains emphasized in addition to appropriate glove use.
rationale_incorrect.D: Home wound-care teaching includes hand hygiene rather than limiting it to inpatient settings.

stem: When reinforcing infection-prevention teaching for a recipient with seasonal rhinitis, which hand-hygiene step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Wash hands after contact with excretions or secretions, including nasal secretions
Nasal secretions never require hand-washing in transplant recipients
Only laboratory staff must wash hands after secretions contact
Secretions contact requires stopping immunosuppression temporarily

explanation.rationale_correct: Hand-hygiene teaching includes washing after contact with any excretions or secretions, including nasal secretions, along with other high-risk exposures such as wounds and animals.

rationale_incorrect.B: Nasal secretions are specifically listed among exposures requiring hand-washing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Recipients themselves should practice hand hygiene after secretions contact.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression continues as prescribed; infection prevention emphasizes hygiene rather than stopping therapy.

stem: A transplant recipient planning summer recreation asks about water-related infection prevention. Which teaching point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Assess cleanliness of pools, lakes, rivers, and the ocean prior to entering
Any natural or recreational water is always safe without assessment
Swimming is permanently contraindicated after every transplant
Only ocean water requires assessment; pools and lakes never do

explanation.rationale_correct: Waterborne infection-prevention teaching includes assessing cleanliness of pools, lakes, rivers, and the ocean prior to entering, along with avoiding swallowing untreated water and observing boil-water advisories.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cleanliness assessment is recommended rather than assuming all recreational water is safe.
rationale_incorrect.C: Guidance emphasizes precautions and assessment rather than permanent prohibition of all swimming.
rationale_incorrect.D: Pools, lakes, rivers, and the ocean are all included in cleanliness assessment teaching.

stem: A coordinator is updating hand-hygiene and animal-safety teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should wash hands before and after touching wounds or mucous membranes.
Recipients should wash hands after contact with secretions, including nasal secretions.
Recipients should avoid contact with pets or other animals with diarrhea.
Hand-washing after wound care is unnecessary if gloves were worn briefly.

explanation.rationale_correct: Wound and secretion hand-washing and avoiding animals with diarrhea are supported. Statement IV is false because hand-washing before and after wound contact is specifically recommended regardless of brief glove use.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—contact with animals with diarrhea should be avoided.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because wound-contact hand-washing remains recommended.
